claims.text: What the image looks like Pleural-based mass w effusion ± plaques → mesothelioma
claims.quote: Pleural-based mass with effusion ± plaques Mesothelioma
claims.locator: Chest X-Ray (CXR), Chronic / Diffuse Lung Disease table

claims.text: Aspects (abnorm in red) Effusions / everything else: pleural lines, thickening, fluid
claims.quote: E - Effusions / Everything else: pleural lines, thickening, fluid.
claims.locator: Chest X-Ray (CXR), Reading Approach (RIPE technical adequacy → ABCDE-FGHI)

claims.text: Typical CXR: nodular pleural thickening, pleural effusion and loss of thoracic vol
claims.quote: Typical findings on chest x-ray are nodular pleural thickening, pleural effusion, and loss of thoracic volume.

claims.text: Chest CT shows the pleural chgs and extent of dz better; PET-CT and MRI may help identify more extensive dz
claims.quote: Chest CT enables better visualization of the pleural changes and extent of the disease. PET-CT and MRI scanning may help identify more extensive disease.

claims.text: Eti A rare, primary CA of the mesothelial serosa, caused by asbestos exposure in the great majority of cases
claims.quote: Pleural mesothelioma, a rare, primary cancer of mesothelial serosa, is caused by asbestos exposure in the great majority of cases.

claims.text: The asbestos exposure can be occupational, para-occupational or enviro
claims.quote: The great majority of malignant mesotheliomas are related to asbestos exposure, which can be occupational, para-occupational, or from environmental sources.

claims.text: Sx Pts most often present w dyspnea and nonpleuritic CP; pleural effusions, USU unilat and hemorrhagic, are present in up to 90%; constitutional Sx are uncommon @ presentation
claims.quote: Patients most often present with dyspnea and nonpleuritic chest pain. Pleural effusions, usually unilateral and hemorrhagic, are present in up to 90% of patients. Constitutional symptoms are uncommon at presentation.

claims.text: Invasion of the chest wall and adjacent structures may cause severe pain, hoarseness, dysphagia, brachial plexopathy or ascites
claims.quote: Tumor invasion of the chest wall and other adjacent structures may cause severe pain, hoarseness, dysphagia, brachial plexopathy, or ascites.

claims.text: Tx and next step Her chart: thoracoscopic bx
claims.locator: Chest X-Ray (CXR), Chronic / Diffuse Lung Disease table

claims.text: A pleural bx = USU required, b/c pleural fluid cytology = USU nondiagnostic
claims.quote: A pleural biopsy is usually required as pleural fluid cytology is usually nondiagnostic.

claims.text: Rare, aggressive and almost always fatal; 5-year survival about 10%
claims.quote: Malignant mesothelioma is a rare, aggressive, and almost always fatal cancer, with a 5-year survival rate of about 10%.

claims.text: Tx focuses on supportive care; immunotx has shown promise, but prognosis remains poor
claims.quote: Treatment is focused on supportive care. Although immunotherapy has shown promise, prognosis remains poor.
